Each entry was traced against server.js at the line cited, 2026-07-31 (batch-10).

exemptions.rationale: C51 §3.1.2.2 CSP violation sink. The browser's CSP reporting agent posts these; the User-Agent cannot attach a Bearer token, so requiring auth would disable the report channel entirely. Writes no database row and no user-attributed state — the handler answers 204 and rate-caps console telemetry. Nothing an anonymous caller submits is persisted or read back. (server.js:377)

IP-A3 A.5.e RAC onboarding lead capture. Deliberately pre-authentication: the visitor has not signed up yet, so there is no session to require. The row is a self-attributed marketing lead with no tenant, no project and no permission consequence; it is never read back into an authorisation decision. Rate-capped + size-capped by leadsBodyParser. (server.js:383)

§OVERPASS-PROXY. POST only because Overpass-QL is sent in the body; semantically a READ-THROUGH cache of public OpenStreetMap data. Persists nothing user-attributed — the cache key is the query, the value is public OSM geometry identical for every caller. Guarded by apiLimiter (60/min/IP) + globalLimiter. (server.js:395)

Internal plan-provisioning hook. Gated on the x-internal-secret header matching INTERNAL_PLAN_SECRET, and FAIL-CLOSED: when the env var is unset the first condition is falsy and every request gets 403, so an unconfigured deployment denies rather than accepts. Not a session route — the caller is a backend, which has no user session to present. (server.js:1800)

Account creation. Authentication cannot precede the creation of the account it would authenticate. The write is confined to a new self-owned pryzm_users row; the caller cannot name an existing tenant or project. (server.js:1881)

Credential exchange — the route that MINTS the session, so it cannot require one. POST only because the password travels in the body; it mutates no domain state, it verifies a hash and issues a JWT. (server.js:1904)

Stripe calls this server-to-server and has no PRYZM session. Authenticated by a STRONGER mechanism than authMiddleware: constructWebhookEvent() HMAC-verifies the raw body against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET before ANY business logic, a missing stripe-signature header is 400, and a missing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY/STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is 503 (fail-closed, and 5xx so Stripe retries rather than silently dropping a paid subscription). Verified by reading the handler, not by trusting the previous matrix's claim. (server.js:2078)
